title: Rate limiting across many servers

kcs.statement: When N gateway instances enforce one limit with local counters, a client can exceed the limit by up to N times; a shared counter store (e.g. an in-memory key-value store) keeps one global count.
Read-then-write counter updates race under concurrency, so two requests can both take the last slot; an atomic increment, or one script that checks and updates together, prevents this.

problem_ideas: 10 gateway nodes each allow 100/min locally: what is the worst-case global rate for one user?
Trace two concurrent requests through GET-then-SET on a counter at 99/100 and show both passing
A shared counter store adds 1 ms per request: what does that cost at 50,000 QPS of gateway traffic?
The shared counter store goes down: fail open or fail closed, for a public API and for a login endpoint?
Propose local pre-limiting with periodic sync and state its accuracy trade-off
Multi-region: should limits be global or per region? Argue with a latency number
